newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae sets first stg global bond.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae sets first stg global bond.

text.p: The U.S. Federal National Mortgage Association launched the first global sterling bond, joint lead managers BZW and Merrill Lynch said on Tuesday.
The 1.0 billion stg June 2002 bond will be priced on Wednesday to yield 10 basis points over the 7.00 percent British government bond (gilt) due June 2002.
The supranational is rated triple-A by both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's.
The lead managers could not comment on the issue prior to its pricing due to U.S. SEC regulations, they said.
Syndicate sources away from the lead managers said there had been heavy demand from British institutional accounts.
Japan has a public holiday -- National Foundation Day -- but investors are expected to purchase paper overnight.
"The deal is being marketed as a surrogate gilt," a dealer said, adding Fannie Mae had probably been attracted by arbitrage opportunities in the sector.

The high-yielding sterling sector has recently seen a spate of new issues. Earlier in the year the European Investment Bank (EIB) launched a 500 million stg June 2002 Eurobond to yield two basis points over the 7.0 percent June 2002 gilt via BZW and Salomon Brothers.
Meanwhile sterling powered ahead against the mark on Tuesday to set a fresh 52-month high of 2.7460 marks.

Traders said sterling benefits from its status as a "safe haven" currency, unlikely to join European economic and monetary union at the outset. Also, Britain currently boasts one of the strongest growth rates among major economic powers and interest rates are expected to rise over coming months.
